attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his Substack post. They are not a quote of Booch, Orosz or anyone else.

semantics.note: The draft keeps 'apparently', 'don't always' and the backup example. It is a hedged observation about coding agents, with no horizon.

contract.note: 'Apparently' marks the claim as tentative and second-hand. Treating it as hedged and not scored is a fair, ordinary reading. Scoring it as a firm assertion would remove the speaker's qualifier.

reviews.rationale: The claim is qualified by 'apparently', so under the hedging rule it is not scored. The packet has no evidence items: the one incident report it found could not be read, so nothing supports or contradicts the claim. Even without the hedge, the packet would not settle it. Not adjudicable.
